fact: DZWatch reports the inauguration of the I-Cloud sovereign data centre in the Akbou industrial zone (Bejaia), presided by the Knowledge Economy Minister, offering cloud hosting and computing to startups and SMEs; the inauguration date is not stated, so the article's 2026-10-04 date is used.
The Constantine data centre, inaugurated in February 2023 and run by Algerie Telecom, offers businesses and economic actors of the region a secure cloud platform.

Iconsnet operates two data centres, in Algiers and Oran, offering cloud computing and off-site backup; the article lists it among operators and private hosts selling colocation, dedicated servers and cloud (no date given, article of 2026-07-05).
The Constantine data centre has been operational since 2023, with cloud platforms for storing and processing the data of economic enterprises.

Algerie Telecom, the state telco, inaugurated its new Constantine data centre, built by its own teams and equipped with a cloud platform for collecting, processing and storing enterprise data; the document gives no event date beyond 'today' in a statement made 'this week', so its published date 2023-03-01 is used.

Algerie360's interview with AYRADE's founder describes AYRADE as a sovereign cloud operator with 3,700 active cloud customers and two operational data centres on national territory (facilities not named); the article gives no date for this, so its published date 2026-06-04 is used.

In a June 2026 interview AYRADE's founder and chairman says AYRADE designs, integrates and operates two data centres in Algeria, for its own needs and as integrator for national clients, and that they are Algerian, run by Algerian teams under Algerian law; AYRADE is an Algerian joint-stock company based in Mohammadia, Algiers, opening 20% of its capital to the public on the Algiers Bourse. Dated by the article's published date.

Ayrade, an Algerian operator listing on the Algiers stock exchange, says it operates two data centres, in Algiers and Oran, and sells sovereign cloud services to more than 10,000 business and institutional clients (El Watan, launch ceremony of 31 May 2026).

BTW Media reports that ADEX Technology operates its own data centre at Sidi Abdellah, certified by ARPCE since June 2020 and described as Tier II-ready, and sells ADEXCLOUD IaaS to SMEs, corporates and government agencies; no date of operation is given beyond the article's own publication date of 2025-07-15, which is used.

ICOSNET's technical sheet describes its operating Oran data centre at Bir El Djir as a 120 m2 colocation site with a 99.98% SLA, 2x100 kVA generators and international links over three subsea cables; the sheet gives no event date, so its 2021-11-16 file date is used.

President Tebboune inaugurated the National Centre for Digital Services at Mohammadia, Algiers, on 5 July 2026; the article calls it a pillar for sovereign hosting of data within national territory, with two national sites, and for continuity of essential state digital services.

The National Centre for Digital Services at Mohammadia, inaugurated 5 July 2026, is built on two national active-active data centres and runs the network, cloud computing platforms, the national public-services portal and the national database.

The National People's Assembly signed an agreement with the High Commission for Digitalisation to use the state's sovereign cloud resources at the National Digital Services Centre; signed on the evening of Wednesday 3 June 2026 (article dated 4 June).
Data centres dataset: ICOSNET Algiers DATA CENTER (ICOSNET), colocation/carrier-neutral, in service; this document names it (published 2026-03-12).
Le Jeune Indépendant says the state's centre, inaugurated 5 July 2026 by President Tebboune, serves administrations and companies as clients.
Le Jeune Indépendant says the Mohammadia complex of the Centre national des services numériques, inaugurated 5 July 2026, holds Uptime Institute Tier III Design certification.
Le Jeune Indépendant presents the centre as Algeria's national sovereign cloud inaugurated by the President.

Le Jeune Indépendant says the centre, inaugurated 5 July 2026, serves administrations and companies as clients and is built to centralise state databases such as civil status, justice, tax and health.

Louail said the National Digital Services Center provides cloud services to public institutions and administrations so they can host their data and localise digital services in virtual data centres, without building their own, using two active-active sites at Mohammadia (Algiers) and Blida.
